# Architecture decisions

**Responsibility:** index the architecture decisions and their recorded rationale.  
**Authority:** historical decision record.  
**Owner role:** architecture.
**Change policy:** supersede via a new ADR; do not edit accepted ADRs in place.

Use an ADR when a choice changes an interface, invariant, data model, deployment guarantee, or supported workload. An ADR must state context, decision, alternatives, consequences, evidence, and revisit conditions.

Decisions do not override newer accepted requirements. When a decision is superseded, preserve it and link the replacement.

- [ADR 0001: Repository structure](0001-repository-structure.md) defines the one-package framework and role-folder layout.
- [ADR 0002: Clarify the adopted v4 contracts](0002-v4-contract-clarifications.md) reconciles the final API, transaction, and capability decisions without claiming runtime implementation.
- [ADR 0003: Failure rollback, automatic scoping, drain, and hosted trust](0003-failure-scoping-drain-and-hosted-trust.md) resolves the corresponding open decisions from ADR 0002 and requires context-scoped adapters, without claiming implementation or backend support.
- [ADR 0004: Receipt access, revocation, and command expiry](0004-receipt-access-revocation-and-expiry.md) restricts receipt access, preserves accepted work after revocation, and requires enforceable rejection of expired external command identities.
- [ADR 0005: Turn round trips, turn batches, and regional placement](0005-turn-latency-batching-and-regional-placement.md) limits a turn to two database round trips, lets waiting commands for one actor share a transaction, and places hosted tenants in home regions.
- [ADR 0006: Scale rules, placement keys, and query tiers](0006-scale-rules-placement-and-query-tiers.md) adds per-type placement keys and a framework routing key, enforces single-shard hot paths, defines local/group/fleet query tiers, and prohibits database-wide serialization points. Its bucket-ownership rule for due-work scans is amended by ADR 0021.
- [ADR 0007: Foundation command protocol](0007-foundation-command-protocol.md) specifies the first embedded Postgres identity, authorization, receipt, and transaction implementation and its unsupported boundaries.
- [ADR 0008: Foundation identity, policies, defects, and PGlite](0008-foundation-completion.md) completes M0 identity modes, lifecycle policies, creation gating, bounded turns, deterministic `onDefect` handling, System callers, and the shared PGlite/Postgres test boundary.
- [ADR 0009: Colocated tests and a separate browser project](0009-colocated-tests-and-browser-e2e.md) requires unit and integration tests beside matching source files and places browser E2E in its own workspace.
- [ADR 0010: One way to do everything: the Effect-native actor API](0010-one-way-effect-native-api.md) makes `Actor.make(name, definition)` the only actor shape, adds reducers, delivers context as typed per-phase services, removes layer options, and gives calls one form outside turns and intents one form inside.
- [ADR 0011: Direct commands, one outbox, and the performance architecture](0011-direct-commands-outbox-and-performance.md) makes commands direct with the receipt as their durable record, carries every intent and timer in one actor-shard outbox, pipelines turn batches, and records reducers, read-your-writes queries, compressed and cold state, single durability, operations, and simulation testing (dictionary requirement amended by ADR 0017). Its relay-per-owned-bucket rule is amended by ADR 0021.
- [ADR 0012: Workflow storage, internal commands, effect routes, defects, merging, and home regions](0012-workflows-internals-effects-defects-merging-regions.md) adds a framework `WorkflowEngine` on the owner's shard, an `internal` definition section, declared `onSuccess`/`onDeadLetter` effect routes, telemetry-only defects, never-waiting commutative merges, and operator-assigned home regions. Its effect-route rule (§3) is amended by ADR 0024, which adds `onCancelled`.
- [ADR 0013: Reconcile the shipped M0 code with ADRs 0010–0012](0013-m0-reconciliation.md) moves the implemented foundation to the one-object `Actor.make`, input-only handlers with a per-actor `X.Turn`, `X.create()`-only minting, ambient caller and tenant, telemetry-only defects, and direct commands with no Cluster message storage (its "Not implemented" list is corrected by ADR 0017).
- [ADR 0014: Adoption, observation, and client reach](0014-adoption-observation-and-client-reach.md) makes existing Postgres adoption, query observation, offline command replay, workflow compatibility checks, inspection/export, generated protocols, and scale-to-zero runner support the next product differentiators.
- [ADR 0015: Durable agent runtime boundary](0015-durable-agent-runtime-boundary.md) (superseded by ADR 0017) defined an agent runtime as an actor-native control plane with durable business state and replaceable sandbox compute, without making an AI-specific runtime part of the core actor package.
- [ADR 0016: Generated durable applications](0016-generated-durable-applications.md) records dynamic applications as a gated product direction: generate contracts and handlers, validate them, and activate them behind tenant isolation rather than executing arbitrary generated servers by default.
- [ADR 0017: M1 record corrections](0017-m1-record-corrections.md) marks ADR 0013's unimplemented list as stale, supersedes ADR 0015 because Outlast is a separate product, amends state storage to plain zstd with a stored codec version, and accepts `placement: "tenant" | "actor"`.
- [ADR 0018: Benchmark harness and committed results](0018-benchmark-harness-and-results.md) places the `bun run bench` harness in `tooling/benchmarks/` and keeps its immutable, machine-labelled result files in a top-level `benchmarks/` directory.
- [ADR 0019: Runner capacity and Postgres pool size](0019-runner-capacity-and-pool-size.md) makes the runner's activation limit the `maxResidentActors` option, reports reaching it as the typed, retryable `RunnerAtCapacity` instead of `MailboxFull`, and defaults the Postgres pool to 50 connections.
- [ADR 0020: The two-round-trip turn pipeline](0020-two-round-trip-turn-pipeline.md) sends each turn as two pipelined statement groups on a turn-owned multiplexed `@effect/sql-pg` connection, keeps contract 02's order, and rejects the optimistic one-round-trip fast path.
- [ADR 0021: Multi-runner relay, effect executors, singletons, and cron](0021-multi-runner-relay-singleton-and-cron.md) (accepted 2026-09-26) lets every runner claim due outbox rows with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` and a lease instead of owning buckets, moves effect executors to a per-runner pool with renewed leases, makes effect timings policy, backs off rows that die unsettled, keeps post-commit wakes local, and runs cron as keyed self-timers the relay rewrites; it uses `0011_relay`, and cron needs no migration. Its settle rule is amended by ADR 0024, which routes a cancelled effect's first success to `onCancelled`. Its cron tick key and UTC-only rule are amended by ADR 0042.
- [ADR 0022: Workflow engine storage, runs, owner-event waits, and version markers](0022-workflow-engine-storage-and-version-markers.md) (accepted 2026-09-26) settles the `0012_workflows` schema, execution ids, `WorkflowRun`, the `waitFor` race, activity call identity, retention, typed step constructors, `wf.version`, and the deploy compatibility check.
- [ADR 0023: Connections, parking, and streams](0023-connections-parking-and-streams.md) (accepted 2026-09-26) puts sockets in a per-runner transport, stores connection sessions in `actor_connections`, wakes parked actors on frames and on any turn that broadcasts, stamps frames with a flushed-through event cursor, resyncs connections in place with a `Resync` frame after an ungraceful owner death, sets the revocation bound to `policy.reauthorizeEvery` (60 s), ends slow sessions explicitly, and keeps an activation resident while a stream is open; it uses `0014_connections`.
- [ADR 0024: Effect cancellation and per-actor effect concurrency](0024-effect-cancellation-and-per-actor-concurrency.md) (accepted 2026-09-28) adds keyed effects with `turn.cancelEffect`, deletes never-attempted effects, reports every attempted cancelled effect once through `onCancelled` (ambiguous when the provider may have applied it) and never retries it, caps running attempts per actor and effect type across runners, and leaves deployment-wide limits out; it uses `0015_effect_control`.
- [ADR 0025: `turn.mint`](0025-turn-mint.md) (accepted 2026-09-28) adds `turn.mint(Child)` on `X.Turn`, deriving a UUIDv8 from SHA-256 over the tenant, parent type and id, command id, call ordinal, and child type; the child is created only by a same-turn creating intent whose System caller carries a mint proof the child re-derives; it amends ADR 0010 and ADR 0013 (`X.create()` is no longer the only minting path) and needs no migration.
- [ADR 0026: Cross-actor event subscriptions](0026-cross-actor-event-subscriptions.md) (accepted 2026-09-26) delivers committed events to subscriber actors as receipt-deduplicated System command turns through the outbox relay, with fan-out after commit, per-source order, subscriber cursors, bounded retention holds with explicit gaps, and same-tenant scope.
- [ADR 0027: The served protocol: HTTP, WebSocket, SSE, and OpenAPI](0027-served-protocol.md) (accepted 2026-09-26) routes one path per public member, carries v1 command ids in `Idempotency-Key` minted against the database clock, authenticates at the edge through `Actor.auth` providers, maps every failure to a status and close code with `retryAfter`, reserves read-your-writes tokens, derives OpenAPI from the served `HttpApi`, and carries ADR 0023's connections over WebSocket and durable event feeds over SSE.
- [ADR 0028: SQL inspection views over runtime tables](0028-sql-inspection-views.md) (accepted 2026-09-28) adds the `durable` schema of versioned, read-only views over actors, state, receipts, events, outbox, timers, effects, dead letters, and workflow executions and steps in `0013_inspection_views`, makes every exposed column public contract, keeps rows tenant-labelled with enforcement deferred to RLS, and grants a read-only role only the schema.
- [ADR 0029: Licence, package name, and release policy](0029-licence-package-name-and-release-policy.md) (accepted 2026-09-26) licenses the whole repository under Apache-2.0, renames the framework to `@durable-actors/core` with the same four entries while it stays in `packages/durable-actors`, sets which packages publish and what they declare, and starts published versions at `0.1.0-alpha.0` on the `alpha` dist-tag.
- [ADR 0030: Executor progress frames](0030-executor-progress-frames.md) (accepted 2026-09-28) adds a `progress` schema to `Actor.effect` and `X.Executor.progress`, sends best-effort, coalesced, per-attempt-sequenced frames through the owner activation to opted-in connections (the performer's by default) and `read.progress` in stream handlers, drops frames after the effect's route or cancellation commits, never persists them or lets them close a session, amends ADR 0027's WebSocket progress rule and ADR 0023's cold connection-list load, and needs no migration.
- [ADR 0031: Hosted ingress, the tenant directory, and regions](0031-hosted-ingress-tenant-directory-and-regions.md) (proposed 2026-09-28) authenticates hosted requests only at the edge, forwards them to any ready runner in the tenant's home region under an Ed25519 assertion bound to a canonical request string, the deployment, and the region, rotates and revokes edge keys through a polled key set, re-asserts streaming sessions through the edge while holders stay in runners, keeps the tenant directory in the control plane behind a per-tenant `TenantHome` actor with absent rows meaning the primary region, places each tenant's singleton in its home region, designs operator tenant moves for L.1, and needs no framework migration in M4.
- [ADR 0032: Event and effect payload evolution](0032-event-and-effect-payload-evolution.md) (proposed 2026-09-28) gives `Actor.Event` and `Actor.effect` a migration chain like state's, stores a payload version beside each event, effect row, and dead letter, upcasts on every read without rewriting history, refuses a deploy that would strand a retained version or roll back past one, writes the old version during two-phase rolling deploys, leaves command inputs and receipts additive-only, and needs one migration numbered at acceptance.
- [ADR 0033: Parent-actor placement](0033-parent-actor-placement.md) (proposed 2026-09-28) adds `placement: { parent: P }` for children of actor-placed parents up to four levels deep, carries the parent's id inside the child's id as `c1.<len>.<parent>.<local>` so routing needs no lookup, gives a family its root's routing key so parent-child intents are same-shard and `group` reads the family in one snapshot, records `parent_type` in `actor_placements`, grants no authority, and needs one migration numbered at acceptance.
- [ADR 0034: Tenant-scoped content-addressed blobs](0034-tenant-scoped-content-addressed-blobs.md) (proposed 2026-09-28) adds `Actor.content` entries that reference immutable SHA-256-addressed content stored once per tenant on the tenant's routing key, uploads outside turns and attaches in turns through tenant-bound, expiring HMAC grants so a hash alone never grants access, writes references only on the actor's shard and reads bytes only off-turn, collects content by a grant-gated mark and sweep with no reference counts, never deduplicates across tenants, and uses the reserved `0020_content_blobs`.
- [ADR 0035: PGlite as an embedded production backend](0035-pglite-embedded-production-backend.md) (proposed 2026-09-28) supports file-backed PGlite in production for one process on a local Linux or macOS filesystem, enforces one process per `dataDir` with a kernel `flock` that a crash releases, claims process-crash recovery but not power-loss durability, refuses `relaxedDurability` and a `dataDir` from another Postgres major with typed startup errors, backs up by stopped copy (an in-process `pg_dump` waits for a compatible build), states its single-connection and no-replica limits, and needs no migration.
- [ADR 0036: The cold tier](0036-cold-tier.md) (proposed 2026-09-28; docs only, built as L.2) moves the keyed state and actor blobs of actors asleep for `policy.coldAfter` (30 days) to one immutable object each, finds them through a `$cold` timer staged at hibernation and deleted on wake so warm turns pay nothing, uploads before a fenced flip that sets `cold_ref` on the generation row and deletes the rows, fetches outside the transaction and writes back with the first turn's commit after its receipt resolves, reads cold actors through for queries, keeps objects past the backup window, and needs a migration only when L.2 is built.
- [ADR 0038: Retention cleanup and the receipt horizon](0038-retention-cleanup-and-receipt-horizon.md) prunes receipts after `keepReceipts` but never before their id expires or while an outbox row needs them, prunes events only as a prefix of each stream, refuses an admitted external command whose receipt could have been pruned while it waited, moves every framework clock with `ActorTest.advance`, and bounds queries by `commandTimeout` with server-side cancellation.
- [ADR 0040: Trusted publishing and the first-release bootstrap](0040-trusted-publishing-release-path.md) (accepted 2026-09-26) amends ADR 0029's release step: workflow releases publish through npm trusted publishing with provenance and no npm token, and each new package's first version is published by hand with 2FA before its trusted publisher is configured.
- [ADR 0041: The quickstart scaffolder and its PGlite default](0041-quickstart-scaffolder.md) (accepted 2026-09-28) makes `@durable-actors/create` the private-until-CR.1b scaffolder behind `bun create @durable-actors`, generates standalone `counter` and `chat` apps pinned to the core's exact versions, defaults them to file-backed PGlite with `DATABASE_URL` selecting Postgres, limits PGlite to development and one process per data directory until M4.14, and tests the scaffold against locally packed tarballs on both backends.
- [ADR 0042: Cron time zones, fixed intervals, and daylight saving](0042-cron-time-zones-intervals-and-daylight-saving.md) (accepted 2026-09-28) amends ADR 0021's cron: `CRON_TZ=<zone>` expressions and `@every <duration>` intervals, tick keys that include the zone or interval, a skipped wall-clock time firing once at the first instant after the gap and a repeated one once at its first occurrence, epoch-anchored intervals, and the catch-up rule for both; no migration.
- [ADR 0043: The docs site, its Markdown copies, and `llms.txt`](0043-docs-site.md) (proposed 2026-09-28) adds `apps/docs`, which renders the home page, the quickstart, `docs/api`, and the guides with `Bun.markdown` into static HTML plus a Markdown copy per page and an `llms.txt`, keeps contracts, ADRs, and the rest of `docs/` in the repository behind GitHub links, and fails the build on a broken link or heading anchor.
- [ADR 0044: Blob entry quota and entry deletion](0044-blob-entry-quota-and-deletion.md) (proposed 2026-09-28) adds `policy.maxBlobEntries` (default 10,000) enforced in the `set` and `append` statements, adds `BlobWrite.delete`, and keeps ADR 0038's server-side cancellation as the bound on query reads.
- [ADR 0045: Cookie credentials in `Actor.auth.make` and OpenAPI](0045-cookie-security-schemes.md) (proposed 2026-09-28) replaces `cookies: true` with `cookies: { name }`, makes bearer the default only for providers without a cookie (`bearer: true` adds it back), and documents each credential as an alternative security requirement, the cookie as an `apiKey` `in: cookie` scheme; it amends ADR 0027 sections 3 and 6.
- [ADR 0046: The shared workflow-engine suite runs through engine drivers](0046-workflow-engine-suite-drivers.md) (proposed 2026-09-28) amends ADR 0022 decision 10: one shared body runs on the framework engine and `ClusterWorkflowEngine` through per-engine drivers, because the framework engine is not an Effect `WorkflowEngine` service; `Ship.step` records one row per `Activity.retry` attempt; an interrupted execution replays to its first unsettled step so `Workflow.withCompensation` finalizers run once; the divergences are asserted per engine; a resume preempts a live run parked on a clock or wait that can settle; and a retry window minus `deliveryTimeout` at or below the 30-second recovery interval makes a lost activity's calls end in `ActivityOutcomeUnknown`, which startup warns about.
- [ADR 0047: The billing example is `examples/subscriptions`](0047-subscriptions-example.md) (proposed 2026-09-28) places M3.6's billing example in the `@durable-actors/subscriptions` workspace package, because `@durable-actors/billing` is the control plane's Polar package, and limits it to an in-memory provider stand-in.
- [ADR 0048: Record corrections for `turn.mint`, executor progress, and inspection views](0048-mint-progress-and-inspection-record-corrections.md) (accepted 2026-09-28) amends ADR 0025 to require the relay and the parent's committed intent row for creation, reject keyed creating intents, accept `source: "timer"` on delayed ones, and check non-mintable children at the `turn.mint` call; amends ADR 0030 so closing progress may delay a settle by at most 100 ms, each attempt's last frame borrows against the runner-wide cap instead of being dropped, and `seq` counts accepted frames; and corrects ADR 0028's `scheduled_at_ms` wording.
- [ADR 0049: Observability: stable span and metric names, Prometheus, and defect spans](0049-observability-names-metrics-and-defect-spans.md) (proposed 2026-09-29) names the admission, turn, commit, relay, and effect spans with no ids in any name, fails a defect's turn span, counts turns, receipts, events, outbox rows, activations, mailbox age, pool waits, and relay work per runner, samples outbox rows, relay lag, stuck rows, subscription lag, and pinned events from one runner, serves `/metrics` and `/defects` through `Telemetry.serve`, and has `durable defects list` read each runner's bounded defect log; no migration.
